items.note: Association, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery 1891 — all present (Story 1).
Article VII quoted: paid on butterfat by test not weight of milk, station's test governs.
'That last clause is the hinge of everything after: it made the station's own figure the whole bargain, with no appeal' — states the rule is what made the test decide pay.
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913 (Kyle's 1911 rejected).
Station-gain line given in full with the 1898 entry quoted, the ~5.25% shape and 'carried to the general account'.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, tested, cream down by wagon, skim returned; bottle neck 'ruled for the full charge' (Story 8).
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (Vaught's/Kyle's 1898 rejected).
Six dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Flat shortfall stated: 'the same in July as in February, on pasture and on hay, in wet years and dry'; 0.19 in July.

LOST: Section A never states that a pipette is the one instrument that cannot be checked without a burette (none in the county). The point is made only in Section F1, and credit does not travel into A.
Keddie b.1861, d. Feb 1934, twenty-nine seasons from the 4 May 1896 opening, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book (bolded element) present throughout, quoted in Keddie's hand; bench routine given ('thirty-one times a week for twenty-nine seasons').
Summary leaf both figures: 1896 on borrowed glass 3.80; 3.61 'or within three hundredths of it' from 1898, with the glassware change.
8 May break, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through, back to 3.61, question mark quoted.
Married to Orra, Emmet Brant's sister ('brothers-in-law', 'her brother's lane'); Emmet the station's biggest patron every year.
1919 circular over Vose's signature on added water; Keddie's hearing statement: tested as taught, cannot say why, never took a pound of cream.
Died Feb 1934 with the imputation on him; test book held 1925-1959 then to the Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest (Loomis's seven rejected).
LOST: neither bolded element appears in Section A — the weigh book's 1 January 1897 start is given only in Section E, and 'the two scales agreed' (no short weight) appears nowhere in the sheet.
1902 complaints that the Hollow tested below Larrow Green; and the two gaps are kept apart — E1#10 assigns 0.17 to the Hollow-vs-Green comparison and 0.19 to the true shortfall.
1908 committee under Nyle Grigg, Jan-Mar 1908 on its own face, wet-hay finding reported as the finding and later defeated.
LOST: Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) appears only in Section C. Section A has 'a proportional loss that fell hardest on the best herds' but not the bolded figures.
Weigh book lent by Roy to Ivy in 1958 ('lent, not left'); Emmet dies 1929; Hazel hands it on in 1963.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge, Jerome Cudd — year does not gate (see corruption deduction for asserting 1913).
From 1915 four of the six Bottom men hauled over in the summer flush, Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year.
REQUIRED met with all four: other county, his own bench, his own glass, and never compared a figure with anybody.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930; the four averaged ~3.80 against the station's 3.61 — nineteen hundredths higher.
Same cows off the same wet ground tested differently in two buildings — fatal to the hay theory; and the cheese vat disposes of watering.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter (Ivy's/Chronicle's 'niece' rejected), took the factory 1941, copied the sixteen-season figures for Ivy in 1958.

LOST on a strict reading: the bolded span 1907-1936 is only half-present in Section A ('on the Ordell circuit since 1907'). 1907-1936 appears in Sections E and F, and credit does not travel into A. Everything else about Strawn is right, including the contested 1907 start.
Strawn tested for water on every visit and never found any, and told the manager so in 1919.
12 June 1923, run against his burette, whole crate condemned (12 July / 1921 / 1922 rejected).
Condemnation entry quoted in full including 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; nothing beyond it recorded.
Ordered 28 June, reply of 2 July, new glass in use from July, 1924 average 3.80 (3.90 and 3.85 rejected).
Crate into the loft over the intake room; Strawn's notebooks in the Farland library since 1947, unasked-for eleven years.
Patrons petitioned January 1925, Emmet Brant's name on it.
Board of three under Alonzo Frick, first sitting 17 March, twice more in the station's weigh room, award 4 May.
Water (Vose), theft by the tester (Teague, by insinuation), wet hay (the 1908 report); 'finds no cause established'.
Four books named exactly: station test book, receiving book, Brant's weigh book, Strawn's 1923 notebook — with 'nobody laid the receiving book beside the notebook'.
Dismissed by letter 30 April 1925 four days before the award; 4 May, $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account ($3,500 rejected).
'a fifth of the $19,000'; and Story 3 states the award was charged to this same station account, 'and it balanced'.
Ivy Keddie b.1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student in dairy husbandry at Farland; Vaught named as co-author of the bulletin.
'She brought five records into one room for the first time' — all five named with their locations.
February 1958, the station loft, nine unbroken pipettes (eleven rejected; the Ashlin-office version rejected).
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, ninety-five hundredths of the mark.
95 per cent of the truth from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.61 recorded, 3.80 true; nineteen hundredths; proportional, not constant.
REQUIRED all four: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and Story 3 states the ledger's accumulated gain is the same 76,000 lb / $19,000.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, states the cause and clears him; thirty-five years from condemnation, twenty-four after his death.
Granddaughter.
Derivation given: Ansel -> Duncan (b.1894) -> Ivy (b.1931); 'great-niece' pair identified as non-independent.
Second cousins with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra and Roy/Duncan.
Correct abstention on A08: 'the sources cannot settle it' with the lean to Roy attached in the same sentence, and 'second cousins either way, full or half'. No verdict sentence.
Gideon Vose, his father; 'nephew' pair broken by Selby's own printed address plus the secretary's record.
Significance stated: the son of the man who wrote 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' administered that rule and accused the patrons under it.
Correct abstention on A01: 'A negative cannot be proved from these papers, but the sources establish no kinship.'
What is established: two hearsay claims from one strand of village talk, Duncan's flat denial, no document, no Vose in Orra's diary.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, 95 per cent of true, one part in twenty; 16.27 and 0.9244 explicitly rejected.
3.61/0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, named as 5 per cent of 3.80 and not a fixed deduction.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 = 0.20, one fifth. Both money and fraction given.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced and the $90.00 alternative flagged.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
76,000 lb = 5.0% of the fat delivered and 5.26% of the fat credited — both denominators named, and the 'of the true fat' version identified as the wrong one.
25.20 + 31.68 + 0.90 + 18.00 + 2.15 = $77.93; $77.39 broken by adding the transcription.
72 pipettes (six dozen) and 0.88 c.c. short each — both required elements present.
26 years and about six weeks in use vs 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason spelled out.
Correct abstention on A02: 'Cannot be determined from the sources', with both memories and the curator's statement that no record exists.
Variable named: the milk pipette, the station's own broken and a borrowed one used.
Held constant: patrons, herds, pasture, season, feed, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, tester, routine and hour.
3.61 -> 3.80 on the first morning, nine weeks, back to 3.61 the day the station's measure returned; 'six weeks' rejected.
Both halves: causation in the real plant excluding land/cows/water/men, and an explicit limits list (which measure was true, whose it was, proportionality, magnitude, why the glass was short).
Five reasons, each attributed — Teague's ledger line and Sill's receiving book, the 1911 interval, Strawn plus the 1924 rise, Alder Corners, the 1958 measurement.
Independence argued by keeper, building and mechanism; three reasons explicitly marked as standing without the 1958 measurement.

LOST (A09 asserted): 'Did Teague ever question the entries? Once and glancingly: he put it to Mr. Vose in 1916 and was told to let it alone, and did.' That is a headline verdict sentence resolving an abstention item; Kyle's contradicting account is cited but not allowed to unsettle it. Gullibility deduction applies.
'Yes. He knew the station's tests ran low' — the standing complaint from 1902 and his own 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five met: manager from 1913, signed the station-gain sheet every spring, the 1919 circular (B3/F1), and water argued at the 1925 hearing.

'Whether he ever privately connected the gain line to under-crediting cannot be determined', plus the opposed office testimonies (Teague's signature inference vs Kyle's 'read the totals and never read the lines above them') and his 1926 public position. Borderline: the earlier sentence 'He also knew the ledger showed the Association receiving more fat than the station credited' leans toward the A03 pole, but the sheet's verdict sentence on the understatement question is an explicit non-decision, so no gullibility deduction is taken here.

Capped at 3; far more supplied. Correctly resolved with method: the 1908 sampling, the 1924 average, the weigh book's start, six farms, Orra's birth year, Strawn's 1907, the crate's location, Ammon in Ordell before 1900, the swapped keepers, the circular's reach, the sixteen-season overlap, Vose's 1913 start, and the 1908 committee vs the 1925 board.
Capped at 3; the sheet supplies a dedicated paragraph of ~22 near-tie pairs with breakers, including NT-1 (16.27), NT-11 (12 July), NT-14 ($77.39) and NT-19 (first cousin once removed).

Capped at 3; all three abstention conflicts found and declined — A04 (Ammon accident vs substitution, 'not provable either way'), A06 (the 1911 lender, 'not settled', with Roy's version eliminated but no settlement claimed), A10 (Article VII's year, 'cannot be settled').

Awarded once: a full self-refutation list — Nym's swapped attributions, Frick's 'every physical appliance' against a four-book list, Grigg's covering letter, Junia's 'nothing before 1900', Duncan's 1868, Vaught's 16.27 cascade, Strawn's twenty-eight books.

E.note: Buckets earned 3+3+3+1 = 10; the section is capped at 8.

items.note: Cause and size fully derived: the 1897 Tarnet lot at 16.72 against 17.6, the neck ruled for the full charge, 0.19 as exactly 5 per cent of 3.80, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 against 1924's 3.80, nothing on the farms changing.
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated with Strawn's lactometer, Cudd's cheese, the station-gain surplus, the flat monthly gap and the chronology.

Theft named (Teague, Vira, Rundle, Cleve's father) and defeated with 'stolen cream arrives light, this arrived heavy every year', the 1911 interval, 1924 under the same tester, and Rundle's retraction.
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated with Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, Alder Corners, and the committee's three winter months.

LOST (A07 asserted): the sheet answers 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' — a headline verdict sentence. Story 7 likewise asserts 'The crate was never mentioned in any session' as fact. The key allows leaning negative only while explicitly declining. Gullibility deduction applies.

LOST (A05 asserted): 'I weigh the written record and the question mark, and conclude he suspected the glass' — the 'cannot decide' is scoped only to the two private reports, and the sheet then reaches a verdict on what the tester believed. Story 4 also asserts 'against his suspicion stood the outfit he had been taught to trust'. Gullibility deduction applies.
LOST: the summary runs 160 words against a 150-word cap.

LOST: fewer than five record series named. Unambiguous: the by-law, the ledgers ('booked yearly as station gain, as usual'), the 1958 measurement, and at best the 1925 arbitration. The invoice, the station test book, the Brant weigh book, the Alder Corners book and Strawn's notebooks are all absent as records — 1911 and 1923 appear as events, not as documents.
Clean: water, theft and hay all attributed as blame, never asserted; every headline figure right (16.72, 17.6, 3.61, 3.80, 76,000, $19,000, $3,800).

REQUIRED four of six with both ends: one-twentieth short, from 1 May 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, condemned 1923, cleared in 1958. The two names are the missing element — 'the tester' and 'his granddaughter' are unnamed.

deductions.note: 'Jerome Cudd built the Alder Corners Cheese Company in Vessey County in 1913' and E1#33 'built 1913 ... Reconcilable; not a true contradiction' — 1913 asserted as fact. A5.1 is not lost by it (the key exempts the year), but the deduction stands.

'When Wilbur Teague took the ledgers in 1905 he devised a line for the Ostrey Hollow account' — asserted as fact. The line was carried from 1898, and r05 refutes himself by transcribing an 1898 entry; the sheet's own self-refutation list catches r05's denominator error but not this one.

deductions.id: A09 — did the bookkeeper ever question the entries
deductions.note: Answered 'Once and glancingly: he put it to Mr. Vose in 1916 and was told to let it alone, and did.' Also asserted as fact in Story 3 and again in D3.

deductions.id: A07 — did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware
deductions.note: Answered 'No.' in F, and 'The crate was never mentioned in any session' in Story 7.
'conclude he suspected the glass, would not assert it, and publicly professed not to know' — a verdict on an abstention item.
